target_claim: Let X be a finite generalized simplicial complex on a vertex set V: thus X is a family of subsets of V closed under inclusion. Define its actual vertices by vert(X):={x∈V:{x}∈X}; elements of V\vert(X) are ghost vertices. For an actual vertex u, define del(X;u):={S∈X:u∉S} and lk(X;u):={T∈X:u∉T and T∪{u}∈X}. For a ghost vertex u, set lk(X;u)=del(X;u)={∅}. Call u∈V a cone vertex when lk(X;u)=del(X;u), and let V°(X) be the set of non-cone vertices. Define θ on finite simplicial complexes recursively by θ(X)=0 if V°(X)=∅, and otherwise by θ(X)=min_{u∈V°(X)} max{θ(del(X;u)), θ(lk(X;u))+1}. Here a “vertex of X” means an actual vertex. Then, for every finite generalized simplicial complex X and every actual vertex v∈vert(X), θ(lk(X;v))≤θ(del(X;v)).
